did_you_know.text: Did you know? Micah describes a vision of the “latter days” in which the mountain of the LORD’s house will be exalted, and many nations will stream to it.
Did you know? According to the vision, the nations will come to Jerusalem to learn the ways of the LORD, because “the law will go out from Zion, and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem.”
Did you know? World peace is portrayed through turning weapons into tools: swords into plowshares and spears into pruning hooks.
Did you know? Future security is described as everyone sitting under their own vine and fig tree, with no one to make them afraid.
Did you know? The LORD promises to gather the lame, the exiled, and the afflicted, and to make them a remnant and a mighty nation.

Did you know? Micah places “the tower of the flock” and the Ophel of Daughter Zion in the context of the return of the kingdom and the restoration of royal authority to the kingdom of Daughter Jerusalem.
Did you know? Jerusalem is compared to a woman in labor, suffering pain, yet the prophecy also includes a promise of deliverance and redemption in Babylon from her enemies.
Did you know? The nations gather against Zion without understanding the LORD’s plan, and they are compared to sheaves gathered at the threshing floor; Zion is given power to trample them.

Did you know? The chapter ends with a siege against Daughter of Troop and a blow to the cheek of Israel’s judge, a picture expressing humiliation and danger before the turning point described in the prophecy.
